solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Vehicle one’s taken into allotment? I’m not driving on this

indicators.note: one is taken into the allotment word, so it goes inside

blocks.note: a plot = an allotment of land, with I going in after its P

explanation.surface: Someone parks a car on their allotment, then protests they're not going to drive on the veg patch.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the pilot's-eye view: on autopilot, the human is not the one flying or driving.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a device steering the craft means the human at the controls is not the one driving.

clue.text: Not so fast with stake

blocks.note: an ante is a poker stake

explanation.surface: A cautious gambler tells someone to slow down before putting money down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not so fast' reads as a warning; it is the musical tempo, slower than allegro.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is a moderately slow tempo in music.

clue.text: Regularly observed twitch

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other one

explanation.surface: Someone's nervous twitch keeps being noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads straight as well: a twitch that recurs regularly is exactly what the answer is, while the same words tell you to take every other letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Read whole, the clue describes a habitual involuntary spasm, one seen again and again.

clue.text: Greedy types desire what everyone else has left?

explanation.surface: Gluttons want whatever scraps are left on other people's plates.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition's question mark flags a whimsical description: leftovers are what goes into pigswill.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigswill is kitchen scraps, the food everyone else has left uneaten.

clue.text: Pleasure boat avoiding area that may be packed

indicators.note: the word avoids the A, so A is removed

blocks.note: a launch is a motor pleasure boat

explanation.surface: A cruise boat steers clear of a crowded stretch of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Packed' suggests a crowded area; it belongs to the definition, a packed lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunch is something you may pack to take with you.

clue.text: Told of panic, tears into masses of data

indicators.note: telling is speaking, so what follows is heard rather than spelt

explanation.surface: A report of panic ripping into huge datasets, like a computing disaster story.
explanation.walkthrough: Said together, 'terror bites' is TERABYTES.
explanation.definitionFit: A terabyte is a trillion bytes, a mass of data.

clue.text: Delta split coast

blocks.note: Delta is D in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A river delta divides the coastline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coast' sits there as the seaside; it is the verb, to coast along.
explanation.definitionFit: To drift is to coast along without effort.

clue.text: Set aside deed poll avoided by editor

indicators.note: the editor's letters are avoided, so they go

blocks.note: as printed, before the editor is taken out
ED = editor, removed from DEED to leave DE

explanation.surface: A name-change deed poll is shelved because the editor steers clear of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deed poll' looks like one legal phrase (a document for changing your name); it splits into DEED and poll.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: you set aside time or money for a cause, dedicating it.

clue.text: Commonly suggest, very hungry, such feeding

indicators.note: common speech drops the H

blocks.note: suggest = hint, with the H dropped as in Cockney speech

explanation.surface: Someone suggests, in plain words, that a very hungry patient needs a certain kind of feeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Such' points back at the whole clue: a very hungry patient might be given intravenous feeding, by drip.
explanation.definitionFit: Intravenous feeding delivers nutrients directly into a vein.

clue.text: Superlatively neat, is very keen to stuff bird

indicators.note: stuffing puts one thing inside another

blocks.note: a tit is a small bird, split TI…T around the stuffing
dies = is very keen, as in 'dying to'

explanation.surface: A fastidious cook is desperate to stuff a bird as neatly as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff bird' reads as a kitchen job; the bird is the small garden one, and 'is very keen' is a single verb phrase, as in 'dying to go'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidiest is the superlative of tidy, meaning neat.

clue.text: Figure in great pain, not unknown following year-end

indicators.note: what comes after is placed after the year-end

blocks.note: agony = great pain, which loses its Y
y is an algebraic unknown, removed

explanation.surface: Someone is in great pain at the end of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' is geometric: a ten-sided shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A decagon is a plane figure with ten sides.

clue.text: Firmly held resistance I half-heartedly checked

indicators.note: half of the doubled centre, one T, is lost

blocks.note: checked = VETTED, losing one of its central Ts

explanation.surface: Someone checks the resistance only half-heartedly.
explanation.walkthrough: VETTED's heart is TT; losing half of it leaves VETED.
explanation.definitionFit: Riveted means fastened or held firmly in place, as attention can be.

clue.text: Not in any way practical knowledge being voiced

indicators.note: voicing it means speaking it

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone's practical knowledge is useless.
explanation.walkthrough: The K of know-how is silent, so it sounds exactly like the dialect word NOHOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect or informal usage: 'can't do it nohow' means by no means at all.

clue.text: Voices here beginning to resound, organised in epic style

indicators.note: the beginning of 'resound' is its first letter
the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Voices here start to ring out, arranged in grand epic style.
explanation.walkthrough: Heroic verse is the metre of epic poetry, in English the iambic pentameter couplet.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroic verse is the verse form used for epic poetry.

clue.text: Familiarise upper class after a while with a veneer of loathing

indicators.note: 'after' is taken literally as order in the answer: the upper-class letter is written following the while
a veneer is an outer layer

blocks.note: U = upper class, as in 'U and non-U' speech
loathing = hate, split H…ATE as a veneer

explanation.surface: Getting used to the upper class after a time, while keeping a thin layer of contempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upper class' and 'loathing' paint a snob; only a single-letter U and an outer layer are wanted from them. The veneer is the whole word, split round the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to accustom someone to a thing until it feels familiar.

clue.text: Let more names incorrectly in register

indicators.note: the letters are put in the wrong order

blocks.note: N = name, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: More names have been wrongly let into a register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Register' reads as the list the names go into; it is the definition, enrolment being the act of registering.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrolment is registration, the act of putting someone on a register.

clue.text: Sure path winds around European river

indicators.note: a winding path twists the letters
'around' means encircling, so the rearranged path is wrapped about the European letter

explanation.surface: A reliable path meanders round a river in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European river' reads as one phrase; the European is only E, and the river is in Iraq.
explanation.definitionFit: The Euphrates is a major river of western Asia.

clue.text: Every MP has one small worry

blocks.note: S = small, as in clothing sizes
to worry someone, as in 'what's bugging you?'

explanation.surface: Every Member of Parliament carries some little anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has one small worry' reads as a single phrase; the definition stops at 'one', and MP means Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: each Member of Parliament holds a constituency place in the House of Commons.

clue.text: Period in a hospital at the end, being this?

definitions.text: Period in a hospital at the end, being this?

indicators.note: the end of 'hospital' is its last letter

explanation.surface: A stay in hospital when the end is near.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a hospital stay at the end of life is terminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminal illness or stay is one at the end of life.

clue.text: Blank verse poet puts first

indicators.note: the verse letter is moved to the front of the poet

blocks.note: the Roman poet, whose V moves to the front

explanation.surface: A poet chooses blank verse above all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blank verse' is a real poetic form, but 'Blank' stands alone as the definition. OVID with his V brought forward reads VOID.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an empty space, or as an adjective, empty and null.

clue.text: With regard to Victor, is travel permit coming over?

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed on top

blocks.note: a visa permits travel into a country
Victor is V in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A query about Victor and whether his travel permit is arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming over' looks like a reversal instruction; in a down answer it just puts VISA above V + IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A borrowed French phrase, literally 'face to face', used in English to mean concerning.

clue.text: Wanting bachelor, dated with scepticism and swooned

blocks.note: doubt = scepticism, which loses its B

explanation.surface: Lacking a boyfriend, someone went on dates full of doubt and fainted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dated' tempts as going on dates; it is passé, out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass out is to faint, to swoon.

clue.text: One putting a little colour on new abbey

blocks.clueFragment: One putting a little colour on

explanation.surface: Someone adds a touch of colour to a newly built abbey.
explanation.walkthrough: Tintern Abbey is a ruined Cistercian abbey in the Wye valley in Wales, subject of a Wordsworth poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one particular abbey, the ruin in Monmouthshire.

clue.text: Dull with sleep, past taking in half a play

indicators.note: one word takes the other inside it

blocks.note: King Lear, half of the title

explanation.surface: A drowsy theatregoer sees only half the play.
explanation.walkthrough: B + LEAR + Y: the play is Shakespeare's King Lear, of which LEAR is half the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleary eyes are dull and blurred from tiredness.

clue.text: Nasty argument on appeal that will suit you well

indicators.note: in an across clue, X on Y puts X after Y

explanation.surface: A bitter row about an appeal decision, which may work out in your favour.
explanation.walkthrough: Savile Row is the London street of bespoke tailors, so it will suit you in the tailoring sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Savile Row tailors make suits that fit you well.

clue.text: One accompanying touring team on trailer

blocks.note: a WAG is a footballer's wife or girlfriend, as the press calls them

explanation.surface: A partner follows a touring team on a trailer.
explanation.walkthrough: WAGs (wives and girlfriends) became tabloid news following England's footballers abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a vehicle towed behind another, as a goods cart is.

clue.text: Fleeting little thing thus captured by people

indicators.note: the captive goes inside its captor

explanation.surface: A tiny fleeting creature is caught by a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: A meson is a subatomic particle that decays almost instantly, so fleeting and little.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesons are short-lived subatomic particles.

clue.text: Very ardent to convert to green

indicators.note: converting changes the form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A passionate environmentalist keen to convert people to green politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convert to green' reads as a political conversion; green is the definition, meaning lush.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: lush with growing plants, the colour of fresh grass.

clue.text: Rich filling finally causing a pain

indicators.note: the final letter of causing

explanation.surface: A rich dessert filling eventually gives someone a stomach ache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' seems to go with 'filling'; it takes the last letter of 'causing'. Ganache is a chocolate and cream mixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganache is a rich chocolate filling for cakes and truffles.

clue.text: Reduced share

blocks.note: past tense or participle: made smaller, as prices are
a noun: someone's portion of the proceeds

explanation.surface: A smaller share of the takings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduced share' reads as one phrase, a smaller portion; the two words are separate definitions of the same three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a verb form meaning lowered, as prices are, and a noun for one's slice of the loot.

clue.text: Fatty’s right to avoid one standing bail

blocks.note: a surety guarantees bail for someone

explanation.surface: A fat man has the right to refuse to put up bail for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fatty's' looks like a person's name; 'Fatty' is the adjective, and ’s means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Suety means like suet, fatty.

clue.text: One in a suit apparently wearing a vest

explanation.surface: A man in a suit seems to have a vest on underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' is clothing in the surface but a suit of cards: in bridge, a singleton is the only card you hold in a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A card-game sense: in bridge, the only card held in a given suit.
